newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: CALLS FOR URGENCY ON IMMIGRATION AND RECONCILIATION POLICY
The Federal Opposition says a bi-partisan motion on immigration and Aboriginal reconciliation must proceed as soon as possible, to stem a perception there's little policy direction on the issue.

The Government and Opposition are negotiating a mutually acceptable motion, which would commit MP's to fighting racial intolerance, while supporting a non-discriminatory immigration policy and indigenous reconciliation.
Because Opposition Leader Kim Beazley will be overseas next
week, he's calling for the motion to be put forward immediately.
POLICE INVESTIGATE DEATH IN CUSTODY
Police and prison authorities are investigating the death of a prisoner found hanging in his cell at the Sir David Longland Correction Centre, near Brisbane.
Authorities have not released the name of the man, a
30-year-old Torres Strait Islander.
A Corrective Services Commission spokesman says the man was
found in his single-cell in the high-security B wing when cells
were unlocked this morning. Medical staff were advised
immediately, and pronounced him dead. The man was serving a 16-year sentence for sexual assault
and breaking and entering.
MORE EXERCISE SEEN SOLVING ECONOMIC PROBLEMS
Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge says nearly
A$10 million a day could be saved in public health spending if
Australians exercised more.
Opening an annual science and medicine in sports conference
in Canberra, the Minister said obesity and associated health
problems are putting an increasing strain on the public purse.
KENNETT BORED BY SHARES CLAIMS
Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett, says the Opposition's insistence on pursuing the 'shares affair' simply bores him.
Mr Kennett also feels the Opposition is only damaging itself politically.
The Opposition says the Premier was late in declaring interests in Mayne Nickless, part of the consortium awarded a contract toinstall automatic ticket machines on public transport.
But Mr Kennett says he sold his shares before the company won the contract.
Mr Kennett, who's expected to face intense questioning in
Parliament tomorrow, says he's getting bored by the lack of
strength in the Opposition.
AUSTRALIANS EXPECTED TO ACCEPT JAPAN CUP INVITES
The Japan Racing Association has issued invitations to the connections of Saintly and Octagonal to run in next month's Japan Cup.
The event is one of the world's richest horse races with stakesmoney of five million dollars and entry by invitation only.
Saintly's trainer Bart Cummings and John Hawkes who
trains
Octagonal are expected to accept the invitations today.
